name: South Korea
genZNote: South Korea went from post-war poverty to K-pop, K-dramas, and Samsung phones in one human lifetime — economists literally call it 'the Miracle on the Han River,' and yes, that's a real technical term, not just a compliment.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia, bordered by North Korea across the heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
Predominantly mountainous and hilly terrain, with major cities concentrated on coastal plains, especially around the capital Seoul.
Temperate climate with four distinct seasons; surrounded by the Yellow Sea, East Sea (Sea of Japan), and Korea Strait.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Korean is the official language, written in the Hangul script created under King Sejong the Great in the 15th century — celebrated as a highly logical, purpose-designed alphabet.
Confucian values around family, education, and respect for hierarchy strongly shape social life alongside a globally dominant modern pop culture (K-pop, K-dramas, Korean cinema).
Highly competitive education culture, reflected in intense entrance-exam pressure and among the world's highest tertiary education rates.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic with a single-chamber National Assembly; the President is both head of state and government, elected for a single five-year term.
Transitioned from military-backed authoritarian rule to full democracy through pro-democracy movements culminating in direct presidential elections from 1987.
Divided into provinces and special/metropolitan cities, including the capital Seoul.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A world leader in semiconductor manufacturing (Samsung, SK Hynix) and consumer electronics, alongside advanced shipbuilding and automotive industries (Hyundai, Kia).
Rapidly expanded biotechnology and biosimilar pharmaceutical manufacturing, becoming a major global hub for contract biomanufacturing.
One of the most internet- and broadband-connected societies in the world, with early and extensive 5G rollout.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G20 member and one of the world's most successful post-war development stories, often called the 'Miracle on the Han River'.

Maintains a close security alliance with the United States, including stationed US troops, due to the unresolved state of war with North Korea (only an armistice, not a peace treaty, was signed in 1953).
Active member of the OECD and a major contributor to international development assistance.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and South Korea share a 'Special Strategic Partnership', with growing defence, trade, and technology cooperation.
Korean conglomerates (Samsung, Hyundai, LG) are major investors and manufacturers in India, including large electronics and automobile plants.
Ancient cultural links are traced through the legend of Princess Suriratna (Heo Hwang-ok) of Ayodhya, said to have married a Korean king — commemorated by a memorial in Gimhae, South Korea.
Cooperation has expanded in shipbuilding, defence equipment, and critical technologies.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly advanced, export-oriented economy dominated by large conglomerates ('chaebols') like Samsung, Hyundai, and LG.
Global leader in semiconductors, memory chips, smartphones, shipbuilding, and automobiles.
Imports most raw materials and energy, relying on high-value manufactured exports to sustain trade.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The 'Miracle on the Han River' — rapid economic transformation from post-war poverty to a developed, high-tech economy.
Global cultural exports: K-pop, K-dramas, and Korean cinema (including the Oscar-winning film Parasite).
World-leading semiconductor and electronics industries.
The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), one of the most heavily fortified borders in the world.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: South Korea is a highly developed East Asian presidential republic known for its rapid post-war economic rise and global cultural influence.
keyFacts: Capital: Seoul. Currency: South Korean Won.
Presidential republic; single five-year presidential term.
Armistice (not peace treaty) with North Korea signed in 1953; DMZ separates the two.
Global leader in semiconductors, shipbuilding, and consumer electronics.
commonConfusion: South Korea and North Korea are technically still at war — the 1953 agreement was an armistice, not a formal peace treaty.

highYieldFacts: South Korea: presidential republic; capital Seoul; currency Won; single 5-year presidential term.
Global semiconductor leader — Samsung and SK Hynix are central to world chip supply.
India-South Korea: Special Strategic Partnership; major Korean investment via Samsung, Hyundai, LG.
commonTraps: Mixing up North and South Korea's political systems — South Korea is a democracy, North Korea is a single-party state.
Assuming the Korean War formally ended — it did not; only an armistice was signed.
mustRemember: South Korea: chaebol-driven tech/manufacturing powerhouse, presidential republic, major India partner in electronics and defence.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-South Korea Relations
